text: Stein saw the letters match more often when K1 and part of K2 were cut into 13 strands, and wondered whether a second, 13-letter code lay underneath.
Shuffle each text only among the places that share a key letter, which keeps everything the known keys explain, 10,000 times, and see how often the bump at 13 is reached.
K1's bump is unusual (p 0.0075, about 0.02 allowing for the strand counts scanned); Part II's is not (0.24), nor K4's (0.21). A coincidence, closed.
